Every structure pair is fitted on the main chain of an anchor window; each residue's main-chain RMSD is then read in that fit. Rows are anchors, columns are residues. Noise-scaled values divide by the RMSD expected if the residue were rigidly attached to the anchor (anchor fit residual × lever arm), so 1 means "moves with the anchor" at any distance.

Anchor × residue  click a row to read it
median in anchor frame interquartile range expected if rigidly attached full-model fit anchor

Why scale: a short window's rotation is poorly determined, and the error is multiplied by the distance from the anchor, so raw values rise with distance even for residues that move rigidly with it. The expected value per structure pair is σ²·(3 + 3/n + tr(J⁻¹A)), with σ² from the anchor's own fit residual, J the anchor's inertia tensor and A the residue's lever-arm tensor about the anchor centroid (linearised least-squares rigid fit, isotropic noise). The noise-scaled value shown is √mean(RMSD²/expected) over structure pairs, which is 1 under pure noise at every distance (checked on simulated ensembles); the median ratio is also in the tooltip and sits slightly below 1 under noise. Real deformation inside the anchor inflates σ and so lowers every value in that row. Relative view: log₂(median in anchor frame ÷ median with the full-model fit).
